gen-dafont-existence-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Existence has wide, porthole-like counters and terminals cut short of the bowl, giving it an industrial look. Pilcrow Rounded then follows in a friendly sans with tight spacing and big, tall lowercase, softening the whole page.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-abyssinica-sil: Existence draws its letters like bent tubing, one constant stroke width throughout, while Abyssinica SIL slips in a modest thick-thin shift. Industrial meets literary.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-cambo: Existence runs its monoline strokes without a single interruption, set against Cambo, a classic serif with subtle stroke modulation. The heading is blunt and mechanical, and the body is bookish.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-fanwood-text: Industrial and porthole-eyed, Existence keeps its diagonals as heavy as its stems. Yet Fanwood Text, a serif with large-eyed lowercase and gently swelling curves, carries a longer passage along with a literary, bookish ease.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-judson: Tubular, hairline-free and blunt, Existence hits hard up top. And Judson, a text serif with stencil-bold stems and fine hairlines, swings dramatically beneath it, so the page gets both machine and brush.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-manuale: Modern and industrial, Existence has a y whose tail matches its arm in thickness, with porthole counters throughout. But Manuale, a classic serif with a large-eyed lowercase, makes a gentler body, so a bigger heading than body text feels natural.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-naskh-arabi: Noto Naskh Arabic has a very tall x-height and modest, engraved-brass contrast. Over a longer passage that mild thick-thin variation smooths the reading pace, while Existence stays tubular and industrial above it.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-rashi-hebre: This serif reads classic and bookish, with short ascender stems and mild tapering. Existence, with its uniform strokes and no thick-thin shading, sits above it as a blunt, industrial counterpoint.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-ahom: Dignified Noto Serif Ahom brings a lofty lowercase and joins that taper without vanishing. Existence, with no hairlines and no swells, hands over to it like a machine part giving way to traditional, classic serif text.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-noto-serif-armen: Existence looks like bent tubing, with porthole counters and terminals cut well short of the bowl. Noto Serif Armenian, a text serif with big open counters and mild contrast, would feel authoritative even if the heading shrank.
